_comment: Expected SHA-256 hashes for the databases MarkerFinder verifies. Keys are the names verify_database() reports; each value is the combined hash computed exactly the way DatabaseVersionManager.verify_database() computes it - sha256 over the concatenation of the per-file SHA-256 digests of every file under db/<name>, in sorted path order. Regenerate after a deliberate database update with: python -c "from markerfinder.utils.db_versioning import DatabaseVersionManager as M; print(M('db').verify_database('gtdb_markers', 'db/gtdb_markers')['hash'])", or run scripts/fetch_marker_db.py --record.
_recorded: 2026-09-29, recorded for MarkerFinder 0.1.0, db/gtdb_markers = bac120 + ar53 profile directories assembled by scripts/fetch_marker_db.py. Re-verified unchanged on 2026-10-08 against MarkerFinder 0.1.1 (173 files, recomputed hash equals the value below): the v0.1.1 delta is CLI/config, HGT-filter and documentation only and ships no database change, so this stays the reference the release was validated against. A mismatch is a warning on the run path and a FAIL on the --check path — see _note_gtdb_markers.
_note_gtdb_markers: db/gtdb_markers/ is git-ignored: the TIGRFAM/Pfam profiles are third-party work and are assembled locally by scripts/fetch_marker_db.py. This hash is the reference that build produced, so a user whose profiles differ (another upstream version, another split) is told the database on disk is not the one this release was validated against. Severity differs by path, deliberately: a normal run logs a warning and continues (pipeline.py _collect_database_versions), because a different upstream build is a reproducibility caveat, not a broken installation, whereas markerfinder --check scores the same mismatch FAIL and exits non-zero (self_test.py _test_database_hashes), because a self-test that reads green when the pinned database changed would be lying.
_note_marker_hmm: Left empty on purpose: the TIGRFAM/Pfam library used by --marker-mode hmm is not shipped with this release (it is downloaded by the user), so a hash for it would be an unverifiable claim. Note what the empty value actually costs: --check only iterates over entries whose value is populated, so this entry produces no line at all and is silently unchecked (it is not reported as NOT RUN; only a file with NO populated entries at all is reported as INFO 'comparison NOT RUN'), and the run path verifies marker_hmm only if a marker_hmm_dir exists on disk.
